Without such a Mars-Ascendant connection, the native will neither be arrogant nor have egoism. If Mars is in the sub of Saturn, the native will be unassuming and simple — Saturn's discipline and humility subdues Mars's ego through the sub-lord modification. (2) Spiritual initiation (Guru Diksha): 5th house = initiation. Timing of initiation = conjoined periods of significators of the 5th house. Case: Venus is lord of 10th cusp; Venus in Ketu star Saturn sub = will practise. (4) Spiritual progress: 11th house governs progress in any endeavour including spiritual. Significators of 11 operating = satisfactory advancement.

title: Gem/Colour Selection → Sub-Lord of Ascendant + Sub-Lord of 11th Cusp: If NOT Significator of 6/8/12 = Use That Gem/Colour; If Significator of 6/8/12 = Reject
summary: KP rule for gemstone selection: note the sub-lord of the Ascendant and the sub-lord of the 11th cusp. Determine which houses they signify. If neither is connected in any manner with houses 6, 8, or 12, use the colour or gem indicated by that sub-lord. If either sub-lord is a significator of houses 6, 8, or 12, reject the gem/colour indicated by that sub-lord.
full_text: KP rule for gem and colour selection: (1) Identify the sub-lord of the Ascendant (1st cusp) and the sub-lord of the 11th cusp. (2) Determine which houses each sub-lord signifies (through standard KP significator analysis — constellation lord's house, owned houses, occupied house). (3) If the sub-lord of the 1st cusp is NOT connected with houses 6, 8, or 12 in any manner = use the colour or gem indicated by that sub-lord's planet-nature. (4) If the sub-lord of the 11th cusp is NOT connected with 6/8/12 = use the colour or gem of that sub-lord. (5) If either sub-lord IS a significator of 6, 8, or 12 = reject the colour/gem indicated by that sub-lord and do NOT use it — such a gem would increase adversity rather than benefit. (6) Similarly for metal selection: apply the same logic. (7) Fallback when precise calculation is not possible: use the gem assigned to the native's rising sign (Aries=Amethyst/Diamond; Taurus=Emerald; Gemini=Aquamarine/Agate; Cancer=Ruby; Leo=Ruby/Diamond/Sardonix; Virgo=Sapphire; Libra=Opal/Diamond; Scorpio=[not given]; Sagittarius=Topaz; Capricorn=Turquoise; Aquarius=Garnet; Pisces=Sapphire/Amethyst/Aquamarine). Second fallback: use the gem of the favourable planet (Sun=Ruby; Moon=Pearl; Mars=Coral; Mercury=Emerald; Jupiter=Topaz; Venus=Topaz [for Jupiter+Venus]; Saturn=Diamond/Sapphire; Rahu+Ketu=Agate/Turquoise).

result.effect: Sub-lord of 1 or 11 not connected with 6/8/12 = use that gem/colour. Connected with 6/8/12 = reject that gem/colour.

(5) If either sub-lord IS a significator of 6, 8, or 12 = reject the colour/gem indicated by that sub-lord and do NOT use it — such a gem would increase adversity rather than benefit. (6) Similarly for metal selection: apply the same logic. If the 8th cusp sub-lords are the querist's ruling planets: this is NOT the first person for the other party. If the lagna cusp sub-lords are the querist's ruling planets: this IS their first love. If the 2nd cusp sub-lords are the other person's ruling planets: the other party has had prior intimate experience.
full_text: In Horary, how to find whether the querist is the first love of another person? Identify the ruling planets of the querist at the time the question is asked. Then examine the cusp sub-lords of the Horary chart. title: In KP Horary: Use Lagna Sub-Lord Only — Never Moon Sign — Even If Lagna Is Afflicted
summary: In KP Horary analysis, the lagna (ascendant) and its sub-lord must always be used as the primary reference point for the querist — never the Moon sign. The Moon does not move appreciably in twin births, but the lagna sub changes. Therefore the lagna sub-lord uniquely identifies the querist and the specific question moment. Even if the lagna is afflicted, it is still the correct reference. The exact positions of all 12 cusps are also important — not only the lagna.
full_text: Why is the lagna alone used in KP Horary, and never the Moon sign? In a horoscope cast for twins (or for queries asked minutes apart), the Moon's position does not change meaningfully, but the lagna sub changes rapidly. The Moon sign is therefore the same for both twins or both queries — it cannot differentiate. Only the lagna sub changes. Therefore, in KP Horary, the astrologer must always take the lagna and never the Moon sign, whether the lagna is afflicted or not. Not only is the lagna important, but the exact position of all 12 cusps is also important. This is a foundational KP methodology rule — it overrides the common Vedic Jyotish practice of reading from the Moon sign (Chandra lagna).

title: Road to Success: Sign Occupied by Constellation Lord of Lagna Sub-Lord Reveals Native's Weaknesses and Path to Self-Improvement
summary: To identify a person's core weakness and the path to self-improvement: (1) Note the sub-lord of the lagna. (2) Find the constellation in which that sub-lord is placed. (3) Identify the lord of that constellation. (4) Note the sign that constellation lord occupies. The characteristics of that sign reveal the native's tendencies, weaknesses, and the specific improvements needed for success. This is a layered sub-lord technique: lagna sub-lord → its constellation lord → that planet's sign position → sign delineation.
full_text:
Road to Success method: Identify the sub-lord of the Ascendant. Find in which constellation the sub-lord is deposited. Then find in which sign the lord of that constellation is placed. The characteristic of that sign reveals the native's weaknesses and what must be corrected.

1. ARIES: Changes views suddenly without consideration. Dogmatic and fanatical in religion. Loses temper when opposed. Uses militant approach indiscriminately. Advice: cultivate patience and perseverance; avoid hasty action; consider all sides before deciding; control temper.

2. TAURUS: Feelings extremely concentrated, leading to hatred and jealousy. Stubborn, rigid, vindictive — retains grudges for years. Fatalistic. Selfish. Lazy and over-cautious. Advice: cultivate forgiving habit; be active; get up early; forget and forgive others' faults.

3. GEMINI: Prone to sudden changes of viewpoint. Lacks persistence and quick decision-making. Misses opportunities by excessive deliberation of pros and cons. Anxious to see results immediately. Restless; neglects health. Advice: develop coherence, steadiness, quick decision; cultivate patience; take rest and exercise.

4. CANCER: Imagines slights easily; feelings hurt readily. Ponders so long that opportunities are missed. Completely ruled by emotions. Moody and wandering. Anxious about money, ages prematurely. Has good memory but never forgets or forgives harm done. Advice: avoid anxiety; take insurance and recurring deposits; cultivate forgiveness.

5. LEO: Unquenchable thirst for personal glory; over-ambitious even when unfit. Attacks opponents from behind. Shows favouritism; denies others' legitimate claims. Does not consider both sides. Spends beyond means. Advice: cultivate modesty and politeness; cut coat according to cloth; love universally and judge impartially.

6. VIRGO: Chatty and analytical but gives boringly lengthy descriptions. Finds pleasure in criticising others' faults. Nervous and self-doubting despite intelligence. Changes tactics unnecessarily. Consults too many advisers and gets confused. Neglects partner due to over-absorption in business. Advice: develop consistency of purpose; consult one doctor/adviser at a time; forget and forgive; do not neglect hygiene and relaxation.

7. LIBRA: Does not keep emotions in check. Mixes business and pleasure. Wastes time copying others' dress and mannerisms. Unassuming — clever people take advantage. Over-spends on cosmetics and perfumes. Vulnerable to opposite sex manipulation. Advice: make careful choices of associates; know your ability and set limits; avoid excessive company of opposite sex; maintain balanced diet and rest.

8. SCORPIO: Over-estimates self. Does not care for others' opinion. Expects all to be as intelligent as themselves. Over-critical of subordinates. Prone to foul play or unlawful actions under pressure. Risk of alcoholism. Very bad when bad, but courage and will are strong. Advice: avoid sarcasm; do not adopt unfair means; avoid drinking; if a doctor, give minimum doses.

9. SAGITTARIUS: Inherently selfish and inconsiderate. Easily forgets good done by others. Lacks loyalty. Incapable of coherent deception (caught easily). Goes off tangentially in conversation. Lacks purpose and concentration. Wastes energy, money and materials. Hasty in marriage decisions — repents later. Advice: never be in a hurry; avoid over-activity of mind and body; take care of pulmonary health.

10. CAPRICORN: Over-ambitious for money and power. Selfish especially regarding power. Lives on hopes; becomes desperate and broken-hearted at delays or failures. Overworks and overtaxes health. Meddles with others and irritates friends. Incorrigible in sexual matters. Best period comes after age 56. Advice: develop dignity and diplomacy; avoid nervousness; do not be selfish; control overstrain for heart health.

11. AQUARIUS: Prefers solitude; avoids crowds. Becomes lazy and lethargic when alone. Does not follow tradition; acts in unconventional ways. Vacillates and takes long to decide. Cold extremities from sluggish circulation. Advice: cultivate activity and promptness; maintain social standards; give rest to mind and body; walk amidst beautiful scenery.

12. PISCES: Broods over disappointments; becomes gloomy when matters don't come up as expected. Mistakes that those helped don't reciprocate. Sensitive, timid, and afraid of trouble. Seeks advice from many but follows none. Gains sympathy by narrating troubles — weakens own position. Moody. Advice: exert yourself without expectation of reward; be less sensitive; follow the advice you seek; do not belittle yourself.

title: Dasa Interpretation Framework → (a) Planet Nature = How Result Comes; (b) Houses Owned = Source of Result; (c) Constellation Lord = Predominantly What Events Happen; (d) Sub of Dasa Lord: Benefic = Fulfilment; Malefic = Denial/Disappointment
summary: KP's complete Vimshothari Dasa interpretation framework: (a) The nature of the dasa lord determines HOW the result manifests — Jupiter = lawfully, Saturn = by foul/unaccountable means. (b) Houses owned by the dasa lord = the SOURCE or topic of the result. (c) The constellation lord of the dasa lord = WHAT events predominantly occur in that dasa. (d) The sub of the dasa lord: if benefic = native realises the result; if malefic = denial, disappointment, anxiety.
full_text: KP Vimshothari Dasa interpretation framework (four-layer analysis): (a) Nature of dasa lord = HOW the result is delivered: if Jupiter is dasa lord and result is financial gain, the native gains lawfully by honest and legitimate means. If Saturn is dasa lord and the result is gain, the native gains by foul means — under the table money, knocking away without others' knowledge, falsehood, forgery. The planet's character colours the manner of all results. (b) Houses owned by dasa lord = SOURCE/TOPIC: which houses are owned by the dasa lord? Those house matters show the source of events. If dasa lord owns the 10th = career changes; if it owns the 7th = partnership/marriage events; if it owns the 2nd and 11th = financial income events. (c) Constellation lord of dasa lord = PREDOMINANTLY WHAT HAPPENS: the dasa lord is placed in a star (nakshatra) at birth. The lord of that star owns certain houses. Those house matters will predominantly operate during the dasa. The dasa lord offers the results indicated by the houses owned by the lord of its constellation — more strongly than any other factor. Example: dasa lord in Rohini (Moon's star); Moon owns the 12th house = the dasa brings 12th house events (foreign, hospital, loss, seclusion, change of residence). (d) Sub of dasa lord = FULFILLMENT OR DENIAL: if the sub the dasa lord occupies at birth belongs to a benefic = results are fulfilled without disappointment. If the sub belongs to a malefic = results are denied, delayed, or cause anxiety and misery, even when the house matters appear advantageous. (e) Additional rules: if dasa lord and bhukti lord are both benefics AND form good aspects (Western) = native enjoys the result. If dasa lord is a benefic but forms an evil aspect with another benefic = every matter appears advantageous but ultimately delayed/denied. If dasa lord is a malefic in star of evil planet AND bhukti lord is similarly malefic AND they form good aspects = both cooperate against the native = dangerous. If dasa lord is malefic and receives adverse aspect from another malefic = ultimately favourable for the native. (f) Cusp rule: the cusp receiving a good aspect improves that house's matters. But planets connected with a house offer broader results through lordship, constellation, sub, and physical house placement.

result.effect: Dasa result = (a) nature of planet = HOW; (b) houses owned = SOURCE; (c) constellation lord's houses = WHAT; (d) sub: benefic = fulfilment, malefic = denial.

title: KP Rejects Classical House-Lord Dasa Rules (Phaladeepika) as Failing in Twin Births; KP Uses Constellation+Sub for Dasa Results, Not House Lordship Alone
summary: KP's methodological rejection: the classical rules from Phaladeepika (Mantreswara) giving fixed results per house-lord dasa (e.g. dasa of lord of 1 = health/wealth, dasa of lord of 2 = marriage/wealth, etc.) are general at best and FAIL in cases of twin births at short intervals in the same Lagna. KP does not advocate these rules. KP's own method — using constellation lord + sub of the dasa lord — gives accurate results that differentiate between twins.
full_text: KP methodological rejection of classical dasa rules: The classical text Phaladeepika by Mantreswara gives rules for the results of the dasa of each house-lord (1st through 12th). These include: dasa of lord of 1 = health and wealth increase (if Lagna strong); dasa of lord of 2 = marriage if unmarried, daughters, eloquent speech, wealth; dasa of lord of 3 = help from brothers, courage; dasa of lord of 4 = relatives help, land income, conveyance, house; dasa of lord of 5 = children, royal favour; dasa of lord of 6 = defeat enemies, freedom from disease; dasa of lord of 7 = clothes, ornaments, sexual pleasure, pilgrimages; dasa of lord of 8 = prestige, debt clearance, cattle income; dasa of lord of 9 = long-lasting happiness with family, government favour; dasa of lord of 10 = beneficial livelihood, name and fame; dasa of lord of 11 = unmitigated wealth, friendship, family happiness; dasa of lord of 12 = virtuous expenditure, religious acts, royal favour. KP's explicit rejection: 'These are general. But K.P. does not advocate these, as they fail' — specifically they fail when applied to births at short intervals in the same Lagna (twin births). The 12 house-lord dasa rules cannot differentiate between twins who have different life experiences despite identical planets, signs, and house lords. KP's method — using the 4-level signification hierarchy (occupant of star > occupant of house > planets in star of lord > lord of house) combined with the sub of the dasa lord — correctly differentiates twin outcomes.

title: Classical Dasa Results for Planets in 6/8/12 or Debilitation → House-Lord in Adverse Position = Adverse Dasa Results; Avarohi/Madhya/Arohini/Athama Classification of Planet Strength
summary: Classical (Phaladeepika) rules for adverse dasa results when the dasa planet or house-lord is in debilitation, inimical sign, eclipse, or placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house. Each house-lord's adverse results when afflicted are listed. Also includes the Avarohi/Madhya/Arohini/Athama classification of planet strength in dasa. KP does not advocate these classical rules but records them for reference.
full_text: Classical adverse dasa rules (Phaladeepika — KP records but does not advocate): Planets in inimical signs, debilitation, eclipse, or in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house give adverse dasa results: (1) Lord of 1 in 6/8/12 = reclusive life, physical/mental affliction, danger, change of place for worse. (2) Lord of 2 in 6/8/12 = foolish public behaviour, harsh words, misery at home, eye disease, wasteful expenditure, royal displeasure. (3) Lord of 3 in 6/8/12 = death/misery to brothers, bad thoughts, secret inimical activities, insults. (4) Lord of 4 in 6/8/12 = mother's illness, news of death of relatives, sale of house/land, danger through water. (5) Lord of 5 in 6/8/12 = danger to child, mental affliction, deception, stomach disease, loss of energy. (6) Lord of 6 weak in dasa = fear through robbers, danger, imprisonment. (7) Lord of 12 dasa = native spends on virtuous acts, royal favour (classical view — this is the only favourable result listed in the adverse section). Planet strength classification (Athama to Madhya): (a) Avarohi = planet has left its exaltation sign, moving towards debilitation — period of declining strength. (b) Madhya = planet in exaltation sign or friend's sign — period of middling/good strength. (c) Arohini = planet has left its debilitation sign, moving towards exaltation — period of rising strength. (d) Athama = planet in debilitation, enemy sign, debilitation navamsa, or inimical navamsa — weakest period; death may be caused during the period of a weak planet by the planet in the 12th and the lord of the 12th. KP does not advocate these classical adverse-dasa rules, recording them only for completeness. KP's constellation+sub method supersedes these.

title: Kendra Adhipathya → Natural Benefics Owning Kendra Houses (1/4/7/10) = Unfavourable for Health/Longevity ONLY; Malefics Owning Kendra = Auspicious; Lord of 10 Mitigates Kendra Evil; Lord of Lagna Always Protects
summary: KP's position on Kendra Adhipathya: natural benefics (Jupiter, Venus, waxing Moon, unafflicted Mercury) owning Kendra houses (1, 4, 7, 10) become unfavourable for health and longevity only — NOT for all life matters. Natural malefics owning Kendra houses become auspicious. The Kendra dosha applies only to health/longevity; it does NOT prevent the planet from giving the beneficial results of the houses it owns. Lord of 10 (Rajayoga) mitigates Kendra evil. Lord of Lagna always protects the native provided it is not ill-placed.
full_text: KP ruling on Kendra Adhipathya (Kendrathipatya Dosha): (1) Definition: Kendra houses are the 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses counted from the Lagna by sign (not by bhava). Planets owning these houses are called Kendradhipathis. (2) Classical rule: natural benefics (Jupiter, Venus, waxing Moon, unafflicted Mercury) owning Kendra houses turn unfavourable; Jupiter and Venus are more evil than Moon and Mercury in this respect. Natural malefics (Sun, waning Moon, Mars, afflicted Mercury, Saturn) become auspicious when owning Kendra houses. (3) KP's critical limitation: Kendrathipatya Dosha refers ONLY to one's health and longevity. It does NOT make the planet ineffective or undesirable regarding the results of the houses it owns. A benefic Kendra lord will still give the favourable results of its owned houses — only health/longevity is at risk. This is the most important KP correction of the classical rule. (4) Lord of Ascendant protection: Lord of the Ascendant invariably protects the native and improves health and position — PROVIDED it does not occupy the 6th, 8th, or 12th house. Even if it is a natural benefic and thus a Kendradhipathi, the Lagna lord cannot do harm; it is always a saviour. (5) Lord of 10 mitigation: Lord of 10 (Rajayoga Adhipathi) mitigates the evil of other Kendra lords. If a planet owns the 10th and another Kendra house, it gives good results for 10th house matters and reduces the evil of the other Kendra ownership. title: Predestination Principle → Fate Cannot Be Modified by Electing Auspicious Time, Birth of Child, or Spouse's Fortune; All Horoscopes of Related Persons Corroborate the Same Result
summary: KP's predestination ruling: one's fate/fortune cannot be altered by electing an auspicious muhurtha, by the birth of a child at a favourable time, or by the lucky dasa of a spouse. Whatever is to happen is pre-destined and will run its own course. Multiple horoscopes (native, spouse, child, relative) will all indicate the same event from their respective perspectives — no chart can change another chart's destiny.
full_text: KP Doubt 2 answer — Predestination principle: (1) The belief that birth of a child at an auspicious time modifies the parent's fortune, or that a spouse's lucky period compensates for a partner's difficult one, is INCORRECT per KP. (2) Whatever a native is to enjoy or suffer is pre-destined and runs its own course. The birth of a child at a 'fortunate' time coincides with the parent's own horoscope entering a fortunate period — the child's birth did not cause the fortune; both the fortune and the timing of the birth were predestined in the parent's chart. (3) Fate, once written, is never erased or modified by electing propitious times, marrying a particular person, or the birth of children. (4) If 'A' loses and 'B' gains at the races, 'B's luck cannot prevent 'A's loss. (5) Multiple horoscope corroboration: every horoscope related to an event (native, spouse, child, relative) will indicate the same event from its own angle. The wife's chart shows that her husband will go overseas; the child's chart shows the father will go overseas; the native's own chart shows he goes overseas at age 26 — all three independently confirm the same fact. No one chart changes another. (6) Practical implication for prediction: predict from the native's own chart with full confidence — no external event (a new child, marriage, muhurtha) will override what the chart shows.

title: Planet Results Hierarchy → Occupant of a House Stronger Than Owner; Planet in 6/8/12 from Its Owned House = Gives Opposite Results of That House; Strength Conditions for Occupant vs Owner
summary: KP's planet-result hierarchy for multi-house ownership: (1) The planet physically occupying a house gives that house's results more strongly than the planet owning that house. (2) If a planet is placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th sign counted from the sign it owns, it gives results OPPOSITE to what that house indicates. (3) Three conditions where occupant is weaker than owner, and three where stronger.
full_text: KP Doubt 3 answer — Planet results and house ownership: (1) Each planet may own one or two houses. Its dasa gives results of BOTH the houses it owns, coloured by its nature and the house it occupies. (2) Occupant vs owner strength hierarchy: The planet occupying a house is the strongest significator of that house's results — stronger than the lord of the sign. (3) Occupant weaker than owner when: (a) occupant is in enemy sign or debilitation; (b) lord of the sign is exalted and occupant is not; (c) lord is in its own sign (swakshetra) conjoined with the occupant and occupant is not exalted. (4) Occupant stronger than owner when: (a) owner is not in exaltation or Vargothama; (b) owner is not conjoined with the occupant in its own sign; (c) occupant is exalted even if owner is in own sign. (5) Critical rule — planet in 6/8/12 from its owned house: if a planet is placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th sign from the sign it owns, it gives results OPPOSITE to those of the owned house. Examples: lord of 1 in 6 = ill-health; lord of 1 in 8 = reduced longevity; lord of 1 in 12 = cannot remain in own place/spends away possessions. Lord of 6 in 6th from 6 (= 11th) = harmony and profit (opposite of dispute). Lord of 8 in 8th from 8 (= 3rd) = courage and assistance (opposite of obstacles). Lord of 12 in 12th from 12 (= 11th) = gains (opposite of loss). (6) Planet results from a house are also modified by: its nature (Jupiter = lawfully, Saturn = by foul means), its ownership (which source is involved), and aspects/conjunctions from other planets. (7) Lord of a house in the 11th = gains through the source indicated by that house — modified by the planet's nature.

title: Progression = Western Timing Method; Udu Dasa (KP) is Primary; Planets That Are Good in Bhukti Will Be More Beneficial in Their Dasa; Adverse Antaras Become More Adverse in Their Bhuktis
summary: KP notes that Progression is the Western system for predicting event timing (like Udu/Vimshothari Dasa in KP). KP treats Udu Dasa as the primary timing method. KP principle: planets that give good results as antaras (sub-periods) in a bhukti will give even better results when their own bhukti operates in the same dasa. Adverse antaras similarly become more adverse during their own bhuktis.
full_text: KP guidance on Progression: (1) The birth chart (Radix) is the fountain from which life events spring. What is promised in the radical chart by karma will unfold at the appropriate time. Hindus use Udu (Nakshathra/Vimshottari) Dasa system propounded by Parasara. The West uses Progression or Directions. (2) For KP practitioners, Udu Dasa (Vimshothari) is the primary timing method. Progression is a Western supplement. Both alongside Annual Horoscope (Solar Return) are needed for comprehensive judgment. (3) KP principle for sub-period prediction: the results of a planet as an antara (sub-sub-period) in a given bhukti give a preview of that planet's bhukti results. Planets that are good in their antara will be more beneficial when they run their own bhukti in the same dasa. Adverse antara results will be even more adverse in that planet's bhukti. This provides a practical predictive shortcut — study the antara results to project the bhukti. (4) KP notes that a thorough study of Dasa system, Progression, and Annual Horoscope together are needed to pass correct judgment. Separate volumes on these topics are referenced.

title: Birth Time Rectification → Ruling Planets at Time of Analysis Must Match Ruling Planets at Time of Birth; 5 Ruling Planets: Day Lord + Moon's Star Lord + Moon's Sign Lord + Lagna Sign Lord + Lagna Star Lord
summary: KP's definitive birth time rectification method: the ruling planets at the time of analysis/consultation must agree with the ruling planets that governed the birth moment. Ruling planets are: (1) lord of the day; (2) lord of the star Moon transits at analysis; (3) lord of the sign Moon transits; (4) lord of the lagna sign rising at analysis; (5) lord of the star rising (lagna star lord). If these match between the analysis moment and the birth moment, the horoscope is correct.
full_text: KP birth time rectification — ruling planets method: (1) The five ruling planets at any moment are: (a) Lord of the day (day of week); (b) Lord of the nakshatra in which Moon transits; (c) Lord of the sign (rasi) in which Moon transits; (d) Lord of the ascendant sign rising at that moment; (e) Lord of the nakshatra rising in the east (star in which the ascendant falls). Additionally, Rahu/Ketu may represent the planets of their sign lord or constellation lord if unaspected. (2) Rectification principle: these ruling planets at the moment of analysis/consultation should be the same planets that governed the birth moment. If they agree, the horoscope is correct. If they do not agree, the birth time must be adjusted until agreement is reached. (3) Application: suppose birth time is doubtful between 4:26 AM and 5:26 AM. At the moment of analysis, ruling planets are Mars, Jupiter, Venus, Rahu. At 4:26 AM: ruling planets at birth were Sun, Mars, Jupiter, Venus — these agree. At 5:26 AM: Rahu and Venus rule but others do not match. Therefore 4:26 AM is confirmed as birth time. (4) Sub sub lord method: for precise rectification, the lord of the lagna at analysis moment = the sub sub lord rising in the east at the time of birth. Find the exact time when that sign+star+sub+sub-sub rises on the birth day. (5) Additional classical rectification methods reviewed and rejected/limited by KP: Vighati method (multiply time after sunrise by 4, divide by 9, remainder = star trine — useful for confirming star), Mandi-Lagna method (limited accuracy), Pre-natal Epoch (inaccurate — 30-minute birth interval gives only 2-minute difference in Lagna through this method, proven useless for twin differentiation). (6) KP's Vighati-star method: multiply Vighatis after sunrise by 4, divide by 9, remainder counts the star from Aswini trine (Aswini/Makha/Moola, Bharani/Purva/Purva Ashadha, etc.). Adjust Vighati by adding/subtracting 1 until remainder matches the birth star. That Vighati = exact birth time.

title: Hora (Planetary Hours) Framework → Hindu System Uses Fixed 1-Hour Divisions from 6 AM; Western/Chaldean System Divides Sunrise-to-Noon into 6 Parts; Planet Order: Sun→Venus→Mercury→Moon→Saturn→Jupiter→Mars→Sun
summary: KP's Hora (planetary hour) framework: the Hindu system uses fixed 1-hour divisions from 6 AM regardless of sunrise, repeating in a fixed table. The Western/Chaldean system divides sunrise-to-noon into 6 equal parts (varying duration). KP's Modern Astrological Research Institute found the Chaldean/Western method (sunrise-based proportional division) to be correct. The order of planetary hours follows: Sun → Venus → Mercury → Moon → Saturn → Jupiter → Mars → Sun (repeating), which is the alternate days in reverse order.
full_text: KP Hora (planetary hours) framework: (1) Hora definition: a Hora is half a zodiacal sign (one sign takes ~2 hours to rise; half = 1 hora ~1 hour). The 24-hour day is divided into 24 planetary hours, each ruled by a planet. (2) Hindu fixed-table system: uses fixed 1-hour divisions starting at 6 AM regardless of actual sunrise. The planet ruling each hour follows the order listed in an almanac table. At 6 AM on Sunday = Sun rules; 7-8 AM = Venus; 8-9 AM = Mercury; etc. This table repeats every 24 hours. The planet ruling the 6-7 AM slot = lord of that day (confirming the weekday-planet system). (3) Western/Chaldean variable system: divides the interval sunrise-to-noon into 6 equal parts; similarly noon-to-sunset, sunset-to-midnight, midnight-to-sunrise. Each part is a planetary hour of varying duration depending on the time of year and latitude. The first planetary hour starts at sunrise (not 6 AM). The lord of the first hour = lord of the day. Order is the same as Hindu. (4) KP research conclusion: the Modern Astrological Research Institute found the Chaldean/variable system to be correct — planetary hours should be calculated from actual sunrise, not fixed from 6 AM. Hours are not exactly 60 minutes except on equinox dates (around 22 March and 23 September). (5) Planet hour order: Sun → Venus → Mercury → Moon → Saturn → Jupiter → Mars → Sun (this is the alternate-days-in-reverse order from the weekday sequence). (6) Sub-division of hora: each planetary hour is subdivided among the 7 planets in the same order starting with the ruling planet of that hour. Venus hora → Venus sub, Mercury sub, Moon sub, Saturn sub, Jupiter sub, Mars sub, Sun sub. (7) Practical applications: select hora matching dasa/bhukti lord for important actions. Mercury+Mars hora = construction. Venus+Jupiter hora = marriage. Saturn+Mercury conjoined hora = avoid for agreements (effeminate planets, poor for decisive actions). Dasa lord hora + bhukti lord sub = most auspicious time for the event signified by dasa/bhukti. interpretation.detailed: KP Hora (planetary hours) framework: (1) Hora definition: a Hora is half a zodiacal sign (one sign takes ~2 hours to rise; half = 1 hora ~1 hour). The planet ruling each hour follows the order listed in an almanac table. At 6 AM on Sunday = Sun rules; 7-8 AM = Venus; 8-9 AM = Mercury; etc. This table repeats every 24 hours. The planet ruling the 6-7 AM slot = lord of that day (confirming the weekday-planet system). (3) Western/Chaldean variable system: divides the interval sunrise-to-noon into 6 equal parts; similarly noon-to-sunset, sunset-to-midnight, midnight-to-sunrise. Order is the same as Hindu. (4) KP research conclusion: the Modern Astrological Research Institute found the Chaldean/variable system to be correct — planetary hours should be calculated from actual sunrise, not fixed from 6 AM. Hours are not exactly 60 minutes except on equinox dates (around 22 March and 23 September). (5) Planet hour order: Sun → Venus → Mercury → Moon → Saturn → Jupiter → Mars → Sun (this is the alternate-days-in-reverse order from the weekday sequence). (6) Sub-division of hora: each planetary hour is subdivided among the 7 planets in the same order starting with the ruling planet of that hour. Venus hora → Venus sub, Mercury sub, Moon sub, Saturn sub, Jupiter sub, Mars sub, Sun sub. (7) Practical applications: select hora matching dasa/bhukti lord for important actions. Mercury+Mars hora = construction. Venus+Jupiter hora = marriage. Saturn+Mercury conjoined hora = avoid for agreements (effeminate planets, poor for decisive actions). Dasa lord hora + bhukti lord sub = most auspicious time for the event signified by dasa/bhukti. (8) Limitation: for formal Muhurtha (auspicious time selection), hora alone is insufficient — one must also consider the lagna sign rising, the position of planets at that time, and their relation to the cusp signifying the matter and the karaka planet.

title: To Read Planet's Results: Identify Constellation Lord's House Occupation AND Ownership; Occupation is Predominant
summary: When reading what results a planet will give, identify the constellation lord, note both the house the constellation lord OCCUPIES and the houses it OWNS. The occupied house is the predominant result; owned house results are secondary but also operative.
full_text: To judge planet results in the KP system: (1) Note which star the planet occupies. (2) Identify the lord of that constellation. (5) The results indicated by the OCCUPIED house are more predominant than those indicated by the OWNED house. Example: For Taurus lagna, Moon occupies the 11th house (Virgo) and owns the 3rd house. A planet in Moon's star (Rohini, Hastham, Sravanam) gives 11th house results MORE PREDOMINANTLY than 3rd house results, because Moon's occupation (11th) outweighs Moon's ownership (3rd). Also note: one should consider the sign quality (fiery/earthy/airy/watery; cardinal/fixed/common; fruitful/barren; human/bestial) as secondary modifiers in the blend.

title: Rahu/Kethu Priority Hierarchy: Conjoined Planet > Aspecting Planet > Constellation Lord > Sign Lord
summary: Rahu and Kethu deliver results according to a fixed priority: (1) the planet with which they are conjoined; (2) if no conjunction, the planet aspecting them; (3) if neither, the lord of the constellation they occupy; (4) lastly, the lord of the sign they are in.
full_text: As regards Rahu and Kethu: they indicate the results of the planet with which they are conjoined. If no planet is in conjunction with them, they bestow the results of the planets aspecting them. If Rahu or Kethu is neither conjoined with nor aspected by any planet, it offers the results of the lord of the constellation in which it is deposited, and lastly the results of the sign. So one is to include the results of Rahu or Kethu in a particular house along with those of the lords of the constellation. This hierarchy operates in strict priority order — each level is only invoked if the higher-priority level is absent.

full_text: Jathaka Chandrika classifies the lords of houses 3, 6, 8, and 11 as malefics. title: Benefic/Malefic Classification in KP is Person-Relative and House-Relative — Not Universal
summary: A planet that is a benefic for the native may simultaneously be malefic for a relative. Benefic or malefic status in KP is always evaluated relative to a specific person's chart and a specific house or life domain — never as an absolute property of the planet.
full_text: In KP, there is no universally benefic or universally malefic planet. The same planet may bring prosperity to the native while simultaneously causing harm or death to a relative, since it signifies different houses for the native and a different set of houses when the relative's chart is considered. Example: the lord of the 2nd house (wealth/income for native) may also signify the 8th from the 7th (death of spouse) — so it is benefic for the native's wealth and malefic for the spouse's longevity. Similarly, a planet signifying the 3rd house may help a writer mint money but cause separation from or death of a parent. No planet is wholly benefic or wholly malefic; the evaluation is always person-specific and domain-specific.

title: Assess Benefic/Malefic by Constellation Lord's House Ownership Only — Not by Planet's Nature, Position, or Aspects
summary: To determine whether a planet is a benefic or malefic for a person, examine the houses owned by the planet's CONSTELLATION LORD. Ignore the planet's own natural classification, its house placement, or aspects it receives. The constellation lord's house ownership is the sole criterion.
full_text: According to the Krishnamurti system, to classify any planet as benefic or malefic, the astrologer must first identify which constellation the planet occupies, then identify the lord of that constellation, and then note which houses that constellation lord owns in the native's chart. The constellation lord's house ownership determines the nature of results the planet will deliver. The planet's own natural benefic/malefic status, its house placement, and the aspects it receives are NOT used for this judgment. Example: Sun owns the 8th house for a Capricorn native. Stars of Sun = Karthigai, Uthiram, Uthrashada. Any planet in these 3 stars delivers 8th house results for this native. If Mars owns houses 4 and 11 for the same native, planets in Mars's stars (Mrigasira, Chitra, Dhanishta) deliver 4th and 11th house results.

result.effect: Planet's benefic/malefic status determined solely by constellation lord's house ownership — nature, position, aspects are irrelevant.

title: Planet = Source, Constellation = Nature of Result, Sub = Deciding Factor of Favourability
summary: The three-level KP summary for result assessment: the planet acting as dasha/bhukti lord is the SOURCE through which the result manifests; the constellation lord indicates the NATURE of the result; the sub lord is the DECIDING FACTOR determining whether the result is favourable or unfavourable.
full_text: In the KP system, the three-level prediction hierarchy operates as: (1) The planet (as dasha or bhukti lord) is the source — the channel through which the event or desire is fulfilled or disappointed. (2) The lord of the constellation in which that planet is placed indicates the nature of the result — what type of event will occur, which house matters are activated. (3) The sub lord within that constellation is the deciding factor — it determines whether the result promised by the constellation lord will be experienced as favourable or unfavourable by the native. A benefic sub makes the result agreeable and complete; a malefic sub makes it adverse or denied.

result.effect: Planet = source; constellation lord = nature of result; sub lord = decides favourable vs. adverse.

full_text: Example from T08: Mars owns houses 4 and 11 for a particular native. Stars of Mars = Mrigasira, Chitra, Dhanishta. A planet in Chitra (Mars's star) and in the sub of Saturn (where Saturn signifies beneficial houses for this native) will offer brilliant results — gain, success, completion of the 4th and 11th house matters — with neither delay nor disappointment. The conjunction of a beneficial constellation (good house lord) and a beneficial sub produces the most complete and unobstructed results. Brilliant results are obtained when the planet is under the sway of a beneficial constellation lord and also in a beneficial sub.

title: Planet in Benefic Constellation + Malefic Sub → Adverse Results Despite Beneficial Constellation
summary: When a planet is in the constellation of a beneficial house lord but in a sub governed by a planet signifying adverse houses (e.g., 12th house), the planet delivers loss, failure, disappointment, and adverse results — overriding the beneficial constellation's promise.
full_text: Even when a planet is under the sway of a beneficial constellation lord (signifying good houses for the native), if the sub it occupies is governed by a planet indicating adverse houses — especially the 12th house (loss, separation, foreign) — the outcome turns adverse. Example: a planet in Chitra (Mars's star, Mars = lord of 4 and 11 for this native) in the sub of Jupiter where Jupiter governs the 12th house. This planet brings loss, failure, disappointment, separation from partner, partition, and adversity — despite being in Mars's favourable constellation. The sub of the 12th lord nullifies the constellation's benefic promise and reverses the result to loss.

title: Planet in Adverse Constellation + Benefic Sub → Temporary Relief During That Sub Period
summary: When a planet is in the constellation of an adverse house lord but occupies a benefic sub, the native still suffers adversity overall but enjoys temporary relief during the sub period of the benefic sub lord.
full_text: If a planet is in the constellation of a lord governing unfavourable houses (e.g., 6th, 8th, or 12th for the native), it will generally produce adverse results during its dasha. However, if that planet is placed in a benefic sub, then for the duration of the sub period corresponding to that benefic sub lord, the native gets temporary relief from the adversity. The chapter gives the analogy of a camp clerk under a harsh task master: while the task master is on leave or the clerk himself goes on leave, there is temporary peace — but the harsh work environment returns. The constellation sets the overall tone (adversity); the sub provides temporary pockets of relief within it.

summary: For the native's health and longevity, the significator of the ascendant (1st house) should not also be the significator of houses 6, 8, or 12 from lagna. When the lagna significator is also afflicted by 6/8/12 houses, health is undermined.
full_text: As regards health, the significator of the ascendant should not be the significator of the houses 6, 8, or 12 from lagna. Significators of beneficial houses connected with the ascendant and placed in good sub contribute to maintaining good health and allow the native to live long. When the lagna significator is also the significator of the 6th (disease), 8th (chronic illness, death), or 12th (hospitalisation, confinement), health deteriorates. This is the health-specific application of the general principle that beneficial house signification must not be contaminated by the 6/8/12 axis from the house being assessed.

If the significator of a particular house is in the constellation and sub of the significator of the 6th, 8th, or 12th from that house, the planet gives adverse results for that specific house matter.

This house-relative adversity counting is a KP-specific rule that differs from standard Parashari benefic/malefic analysis which always counts from lagna.

If the same planet is in the sub of the lord of the 12th house, no child is born. The benefic constellation's promise is conditioned on the sub being supportive.

summary: No planet in any chart is exclusively a benefic or exclusively a malefic. Every planet carries mixed significations across multiple houses — some beneficial, some adverse. full_text: The KP author concludes T08 with this meta-principle: no planet is wholly a benefic nor in full a malefic. Every planet rules multiple houses, some auspicious and some adverse for the native. Every house in the chart contributes to some aspect of life. If a house is afflicted through adverse constellation/sub, that domain brings worry; if well-placed, it brings pleasure. The net characterisation of a planet as benefic or malefic is a contextual summary of its mixed significations as they play out through constellation and sub — not an intrinsic property of the planet itself.

title: Constellation is the Key Factor for House Results — Sign is Secondary
summary: In KP, the sign occupied by a planet is far less important than the constellation it occupies. A planet in the 12th bhava in a constellation whose lord occupies the 2nd house will give 2nd house results (gains), not 12th house results. The constellation lord's house governs results.
full_text: The sign is not very important. The house occupied by a planet should be judged by taking in which constellation the planet is posited. The role of the sign occupied by the planet is not as important as that of the constellation. Example: If a planet is in the 12th bhava, tradition says it causes separation, loss, and cheque issuance. But actually there may be reunion, gain, and receipt of cheques — because the planet in the 12th is deposited in the constellation of a lord occupying a gain house. The constellation lord's bhava occupation is the determinant of results, overriding the planet's own bhava placement.

result.effect: Planet's constellation lord's bhava occupation governs results — not the planet's own bhava placement or sign.

interpretation.detailed: The sign is not very important. The house occupied by a planet should be judged by taking in which constellation the planet is posited. The role of the sign occupied by the planet is not as important as that of the constellation. Example: If a planet is in the 12th bhava, tradition says it causes separation, loss, and cheque issuance. But actually there may be reunion, gain, and receipt of cheques — because the planet in the 12th is deposited in the constellation of a lord occupying a gain house. The constellation lord's bhava occupation is the determinant of results, overriding the planet's own bhava placement.
interpretation.summary: In KP, the sign occupied by a planet is far less important than the constellation it occupies. A planet in the 12th bhava in a constellation whose lord occupies the 2nd house will give 2nd house results (gains), not 12th house results. The constellation lord's house governs results.

title: Planet A in Constellation of Planet B → Gives Results of Bhava Occupied/Owned by Planet B
summary: The fundamental KP significator principle: a planet A, when deposited in the constellation of planet B, delivers the results of the bhava(s) occupied or owned by B — not the results of the bhava where A is placed.
full_text: The core KP signification principle derived from research: Planet A offers the results of the house occupied by Planet B, which is the lord of the star wherein Planet A is deposited. The planet in the constellation is the significator; the constellation lord's house placement determines what results are signified. This discovery was the result of Krishnamurti's research after observing that planets in the same constellation (same bhava) gave diametrically opposite results to different natives and in different periods — which could only be explained by the sub further dividing the constellation.

result.effect: Planet A in constellation of B delivers results of B's bhava occupation/ownership.

This discovery was the result of Krishnamurti's research after observing that planets in the same constellation (same bhava) gave diametrically opposite results to different natives and in different periods — which could only be explained by the sub further dividing the constellation.
interpretation.summary: The fundamental KP significator principle: a planet A, when deposited in the constellation of planet B, delivers the results of the bhava(s) occupied or owned by B — not the results of the bhava where A is placed.

title: Constellation Indicates the Matter; Sub Indicates Whether Favourable or Unfavourable
summary: The two-level summary of KP result determination: the constellation lord shows which bhava matters are referred to; the sub lord within that constellation shows whether those matters will progress favourably or face obstacles, disappointment, or negation.
full_text: The constellation ruled by a planet indicates the matters signified by the bhava occupied or owned by that planet. The sub lord occupied by a planet denotes whether the constellation's indicated matter is auspicious for progress (favourable sub) or inauspicious so that the native faces obstacle, disappointment, or negation (adverse sub). This applies to all bhava results without exception. The constellation identifies WHAT is at stake; the sub identifies WHETHER it will succeed.

result.effect: Constellation = what matter is indicated. Sub = whether it is favourable or adverse.

This applies to all bhava results without exception. The constellation identifies WHAT is at stake; the sub identifies WHETHER it will succeed.
interpretation.summary: The two-level summary of KP result determination: the constellation lord shows which bhava matters are referred to; the sub lord within that constellation shows whether those matters will progress favourably or face obstacles, disappointment, or negation.

The constellation refers to his health (1st house); the sub signifying the 6th (disease) gives the illness. Lagna significator + sub of 6th house significator = disease during the dasha/bhukti of that planet.

The 1st house constellation identifies the native's personal domain; the 12th sub converts it to confinement, isolation, foreign residence, or loss of liberty.

The 8th sub relates to others' money and transactions (money going to or from others); the 12th sub relates to expenditure, loss, giving away. Both convert the 2nd house financial domain from receiving/accumulating to disbursing.

full_text: If the significator of the 2nd house is in the sub of the significator of the 11th house, there is gain. Of what? Either money, or son-in-law or daughter-in-law, or childbirth to the person. The 11th sub (gains, fulfilment, receiving) applied to the 2nd house significator activates the receiving/accumulating aspect of the financial domain. Multiple 11th-house matters can manifest simultaneously depending on other significators.

title: 2nd House Significator + Sub of 4th (Also 11th) → Property/Vehicle Acquired; Sub of 4th (Also 12th) → Property Sold
summary: A planet signifying the 2nd house in the sub of the 4th lord — if the 4th sub-lord also signifies the 11th (gain) → acquisition of vehicle or property. If the 4th sub-lord also signifies the 12th (loss from 4th) → sale of property with bank position improving.
full_text: If the significator of the 2nd house is in the sub of the 4th house significator: (a) If the sub lord (4th house significator) also signifies the 11th house → the native purchases or acquires a vehicle, car, or house during the conjoined periods. (b) If the sub lord (4th house significator) also signifies the 12th house (other than the 4th) → the native sells the permanent possession and converts it to liquid cash; bank position improves by losing the car or building. The 4th house sub identifies the type of object (property/vehicle); the 11th or 12th signification of the sub lord identifies the transaction direction (acquire vs. dispose).

result.effect: 4th sub + 11th signification → property/vehicle acquired. 4th sub + 12th signification → property sold, cash received.

(b) If the sub lord (4th house significator) also signifies the 12th house (other than the 4th) → the native sells the permanent possession and converts it to liquid cash; bank position improves by losing the car or building. The 4th house sub identifies the type of object (property/vehicle); the 11th or 12th signification of the sub lord identifies the transaction direction (acquire vs. dispose).

title: 2nd House Significator + Sub of 10th and 12th → Property Let for Rent or Land for Tenancy
summary: When a planet signifying the 2nd house is in the sub of a significator of both the 10th and 12th houses, the native lets their land or house for rent/tenancy — 10th (the 4th from 7th = what the tenant takes) and 12th (loss of possession).
full_text: If the sub lord of the planet signifying the 2nd house is the significator of the 10th and 12th houses, the native lets their land for tenancy or house for rent. Why? The 10th house is the 4th house to the 7th house (tenant/counterparty) — what the tenant takes is the 4th of the 7th. The native gives away (12th = loss/outgoing), and the other party becomes indebted (6th from the tenant's perspective). The 10th+12th sub combination on a 2nd house significator thus indicates renting/letting — not a permanent sale, but a temporary transfer generating income.

The 7th house identifies the domain (partnerships, spouse, contracts); the 2nd sub (family, money) or 11th sub (gains, fulfilment) both indicate positive outcomes for 7th house matters.

title: 7th House Significator in Sub of 12th House Significator → Separation or Illness of Spouse

full_text: If a planet is the significator of the 7th house and it is in the sub of the significator of the 12th house, there will be separation or illness of the wife/partner. The 12th house is the 6th from the 7th (illness of spouse) and also signifies separation and foreign residence. During the period of the planet, the native goes away (separation) or the wife falls ill.

title: 7th House Significator in Sub of 1st and 2nd House Significators → Danger to Partner's Life (Maraka)
summary: When a planet that is a significator of the 7th house occupies the sub of a significator of both the 1st and 2nd houses, this indicates danger to the partner's life — houses 1 and 2 are maraka houses to the 7th (7th from 7th = 1st; 8th from 7th = 2nd).

The 1st house is the 7th from the 7th (the partner's own longevity axis) and the 2nd house is the 8th from the 7th (danger to the partner). Houses 1 and 2 are thus the maraka houses counted from the 7th — the houses that threaten the longevity of the 7th house matters (spouse). When the 7th house significator is in the sub of the maraka lord for the 7th, death or severe danger to the partner is indicated.

title: To Assess Longevity of a Relative: Identify Badhaka Lord for That Relative's House; Planet in That Constellation in Badhaka Sub → Danger to Relative
summary: To assess threats to a relative's longevity (e.g., father via 9th house), identify the Badhaka lord for that house. A planet in the constellation of the relative's house significator, in the sub of the Badhakasthanadhipathi of that house, indicates danger or death for that relative.
full_text: Case study application from T10: To judge the longevity of a relative, the Badhaka analysis is applied to the house representing that relative. Example: For the father (9th house), identify the Badhakasthanadhipathi to the 9th house. A planet in the constellation of the 9th house significator (constellation lord = father matters) in the sub of the Bhadhakasthanadhipathi to the 9th house = danger to father. In the worked example: Jupiter is in Saturn's star; Saturn is the Badhakasthanadhipathi to house 9. Hence Jupiter (in Saturn's constellation) in the sub of a planet that also connects to Badhaka indicates Badhaka to father. Note: the determination of which house is Badhaka varies by sign modality (for dual signs = 7th; for fixed signs = 9th; for movable signs = 11th — counted from the house being assessed).

title: Maraka Houses for a Relative are the 2nd and 7th Counted from the Relative's House — Planets Signifying These Are Maraka for That Relative
summary: To determine what is malefic for a specific relative, count the 2nd and 7th houses from the house representing that relative. Planets that are significators of these maraka houses (counted from the relative's house) are the killing/harming planets for that relative.
full_text: For the longevity of a relative, the maraka houses are the 2nd and 7th counted from the house that represents that relative (not from lagna). Example: for the father (9th house), the maraka houses are the 10th (2nd from 9th) and the 3rd (7th from 9th). Planets signifying houses 10 and 3 are maraka to the father. In the worked example: Venus owns houses 10 and 3 (from the native's perspective for father's longevity). Rahu in 2nd from the 9th house (occupying that position) — Mars in Venus star; Mars in the sub of Venus → harmful to father. The broader principle: for each relative, identify their maraka houses (2nd and 7th from their house) and the planets signifying those houses are the killing agents for that relative.

title: Nodes (Rahu/Kethu) Give Results of the Planet They Conjoin or Aspect — Stronger Than Sign Lord
summary: Rahu and Kethu, as shadowy nodes with no sign lordship of their own, predominantly deliver the results of the planet(s) they are conjoined with or aspected by, taking that planet's results as their primary output. The node is stronger than the sign lord for this purpose.
full_text: From the T10 case study analysis: Kethu has to give the results of the planet with which it is conjoined, as it is a node. In the example, Saturn is conjoined with Kethu and Saturn is the lord of the 2nd from the 5th (maraka for children) and is situated in the 12th from the 5th. Hence Kethu in that conjunction delivers Saturn's results — the maraka results for children. Also: 'Kethu is stronger than lord of 7' — Kethu, by conjoining or being in the same sign as the 7th lord, is treated as stronger than the sign lord for predicting 7th house results. The node acts as a proxy for the most relevant conjoined planet.

title: Traditional Astrology Misreads Planets in 12th Bhava — KP Constellation Principle Corrects This
summary: Traditional astrology predicts loss and adversity for planets in the 12th bhava. KP shows that a planet in the 12th can deliver gain and success if deposited in the constellation of a lord occupying a gain house — the constellation overrides the bhava placement.
full_text: The T10 case study (birth 28-12-1900) illustrates that planets in the 12th bhava gave gains and fortune, while planets forming classical Rajayoga combinations (Venus-Mercury Dharma Karmadhipathi Yoga) gave adverse results. This is because: (a) the planet in the 12th was deposited in the constellation of a planet in a gain house — so it delivered gain; (b) the Rajayoga planets were in constellations of lords occupying adverse houses. Traditional astrology based on bhava placement or yoga combinations fails when the constellation and sub are ignored. The KP author's research was triggered by exactly this type of discrepancy.

title: Houses 2 and 6 Together (Plus 10) Indicate Service/Employment; Houses 2, 7 and 10 (Without 6) Indicate Business
summary: The employment vs. business distinction in KP: the presence of houses 2, 6, and 10 together in the significators (or cusp sub-lord analysis) indicates salaried service. The presence of houses 2, 7, and 10 without house 6 indicates independent business.
full_text: From the T10 case study (Service section): Sun and Mercury are in the 6th house (occupation, service). Rahu is in the 10th (career, profession). Kethu indicates what Saturn does, and Saturn is lord of the 6th. Venus is lord of the 10th. First appointment: Sun Dasa (Sun is in the 6th) + Saturn Bhukthi (lord of 6) + Moon Anthra = first appointment in January 1952. The pattern for service: planets signifying houses 2, 6, and 10 conjoining in a dasha sequence = employment/service. House 7 replaces house 6 for business. This confirms the T09-014 and T09-015 cusp sub-lord rules but as a dasha-level timing rule for the first appointment.
